reply:
/plan [what to change] – Update the plan (say what to change after it)
/run – Build: carry on with the plan's tasks
/next – Build only the next task, then stop
/stop – Stop what a task is running now (a command, the app it started)
/retry [task id] – Try a task again
/skip <task id> – Leave a task out and carry on
/undo [task id] – Undo the newest finished task's changes
/goal <what to build next> – Add something new to build
/compact – Sum up this chat in a few lines, so the planner reads less each time
/model [setting] – Which set of models does the work (Budget, Balanced, Quality)
/test – Run the project's own tests
/search <words> – Look for something in every project and the journal
/board – Open the board of tasks
/help – List these commands
/approve [at most $N] – Approve the plan and build (say “at most $N” to set the limit)
/build [accepted | what to build] [at most $N] – Build the accepted ideas, or something new (say “at most $N” to set the limit)
/answer <question id> <answer> – Answer one of the plan's questions
/choose <decision id> <option id> – Choose one of a decision's options
/looks [a starting point] – Make new looks to choose from
/accept <task id> [note] – Accept a stopped task as it is and carry on building
/autopilot on [until HH:MM] [at most $N] | off | status – Autopilot for every project: on (until a time, at most $N), off, or how it is
/pictures – Take pictures of the app as it is now
/note <words> – Tell the planner something: the next tasks and plans read it
/todo done <to-do id> – Tick off one of the project's to-dos
/recall <question> – Look through every project for the answer to a question
/new <what to build> – Start a new project: the planner writes its plan, building waits for your yes
